subject: physics
label: 2022 Sem 1
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Select the correct option for each question. The marks for each question are given in brackets [ ].

questions.question: The deviation produced by an equilateral prism does not depend on
questions.solution: (b) the size of the prism. Deviation δ = i + e − A depends on the angle of incidence, the material (refractive index) of the prism, the colour (wavelength) of light and the angle of prism A, but not on the size of the prism.

questions.question: The refractive index of a diamond is 2.4. It means that

options.a: the speed of light in vacuum is equal to 2.4 times the speed of light in diamond.
options.b: the speed of light in the diamond is 2.4 times the speed of light in a vacuum.
options.c: the speed of light in a vacuum is 2.4 times the speed of light in the diamond.
options.d: the wavelength of light in diamond is 2.4 times the wavelength of light in vacuum.

questions.solution: (c) the speed of light in a vacuum is 2.4 times the speed of light in the diamond. mu = c/v, so c = 2.4 v.

concepts: concave lens always forms virtual image
questions.question: An object of height 10 cm is placed in front of a concave lens of focal length 20 cm at a distance 25 cm from the lens. Is it possible to capture this image on a screen? Select a correct option from the following

options.a: Yes, as the image formed will be real.
options.b: Yes, as the image formed will be erect.
options.c: No, as the image formed will be virtual.
options.d: No, as the image formed will be inverted.

questions.solution: (c) No, as the image formed will be virtual. A concave lens always produces a virtual image.

concepts: emergent ray parallel to incident ray
questions.question: A ray of light IM is incident on a glass slab ABCD as shown in the figure. The emergent ray for this incident ray is
questions.solution: (a) NQ. The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray.
questions.figure_desc: Glass slab ABCD with incident ray IM striking one face; refracted ray MN inside the slab; four candidate emergent rays NP, NQ, NR, NS drawn from N on the opposite face (NQ is the one parallel to IM).

questions.question: The colour of white light which is deviated least by a prism is
questions.solution: (c) red. Red deviates least since its wavelength is the largest.

questions.question: The wavelength range of visible light is
questions.solution: (d) 400 nm to 800 nm.

questions.question:
Observe the diagram which shows the path of an incident ray through an optical plane LL' of a lens. The focal length of the lens is 20 cm.
(i) If an object is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of this lens, then

options.b: the image will be diminished and inverted.
options.d: the image will be real and magnified.

questions.solution: (d) the image will be real and magnified. The lens is convex; an object between F and 2F gives a real, inverted, magnified image.
questions.figure_desc: Ray diagram of a ray passing through a lens at optical plane LL'; the ray converges after the lens, showing it is a convex (converging) lens.

concepts: uses of convex lens, hypermetropia correction
questions.question: (ii) This type of lens (the lens in the diagram above) can be used
questions.solution: (a) to correct hypermetropia. In hypermetropia rays meet beyond the retina; a convex lens makes them meet on the retina.
questions.figure_desc: Same lens diagram as 7(i): a ray bending towards the axis through a convex lens at plane LL'.

questions.question: (iii) An object is placed in front of this lens (f = 20 cm) at a distance of 60 cm. Then the image distance from the lens with proper sign convention is
questions.figure_desc: Same lens diagram as 7(i): convex lens, f = 20 cm.

questions.question: (iv) An object is placed in front of this lens (f = 20 cm) at a distance of 60 cm. Then the magnification of the image is
questions.figure_desc: Same lens diagram as 7(i): convex lens, f = 20 cm.

questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
concepts: SI and CGS units of moment of force conversion
questions.question: The relation between CGS and S. I. unit of moment of force is
questions.solution: (c) 1 Nm = 10^7 dyne cm. 1 Nm = 1 N x 1 m = 10^5 dyne x 10^2 cm = 10^7 dyne cm.

questions.topic: Sign of work done by gravity
concepts: work done with angle 180 / negative work
questions.question: A coolie raises a load upwards against the force of gravity then the work done by the load is
questions.solution: (c) negative work. W = Fs cos(theta), theta = 180 degrees, so work = -Fs.

questions.question: The energy change during photosynthesis in plants is
questions.solution: (b) light to chemical. Plants convert solar energy into glucose.

questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
concepts: principle of moments, shifting fulcrum of metre scale
questions.question: The diagram below shows the balanced position of a metre scale (supported at a point other than the centre with a mass hanging on one side). Which one of the following diagrams shows the correct position of the scale when it is supported at the centre?

options.a: Diagram (a): left side of the scale tilted down

questions.solution: (a). When the fulcrum is shifted to the 50 cm mark, the mass of the left side becomes more than that of the right side, so the left side of the scale tilts down.
questions.figure_desc: A metre scale balanced on a knife edge away from the centre with a weight on one side; four options show the scale supported at the 50 cm mark tilted in different ways. Option (a) shows the left side down. Option contents (a)-(d) are diagrams, not text.

questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
questions.question:
A stone tied at the end of a string is whirled by hand in a horizontal circle with uniform speed.
(i) Name the force required for this circular motion
questions.solution: (b) Centripetal force. The tension of the string provides the necessary centripetal force.

questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
questions.question: (ii) What is the direction of the above-mentioned force?

options.a: Towards the centre of the circular path.
options.b: Away from the centre of the circular path.
options.c: Normal to the radius at a point where the body is present on the circular path.
options.d: Direction of this force keeps on changing alternately towards and away from the centre.

questions.solution: (a) Towards the centre of the circular path.

questions.question:
A body of mass 200 g falls freely from a height of 15 m. [g = 10 ms^-2]
(i) When the body reaches 10 m above the ground, its potential energy will be

questions.topic: Gain in kinetic energy free fall
concepts: conservation of energy, KE gain in free fall
questions.question: (ii) The gain in kinetic energy of the body when it reaches 10 m above the ground is
questions.solution: (b) 10 J. Total energy at 15 m = 0.2 x 10 x 15 = 30 J; P.E. at 10 m = 20 J; K.E. gain = 30 - 20 = 10 J.

questions.question: (iii) The total mechanical energy it will possess, when it is just about to strike the ground is
questions.solution: (c) 30 J. Total energy is conserved.

questions.question: (iv) The velocity in ms^-1 with which the body will hit the ground is
A woman draws water from a well using a fixed pulley. The mass of the bucket and the water together is 10 kg. The force applied by the woman is 200 N. The mechanical advantage is (g = 10 m/s^2)
A single fixed pulley is used because

options.a: it changes the direction of applied effort conveniently.

questions.solution: (a) it changes the direction of applied effort conveniently.

concepts: velocity ratio of pulley system from diagram
questions.question: In the diagram shown below, the velocity ratio of the arrangement is
questions.solution: (b) 2. If pulley B moves x downwards, the rope moves 2x, so velocity ratio = 2.
questions.figure_desc: A pulley arrangement with a movable pulley B and a rope; the diagram is needed to see the pulley system.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the correct mathematical relation?
questions.solution: (d) Power = Force x Velocity.

questions.question: Select a correct option with respect to echo depth sounding:

options.b: the frequency of the waves used is between 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz.

questions.solution: (c) ultrasonic waves are used.

questions.question: Which one of the following diagnostic methods use reflection of sound?
questions.solution: (c) Echo cardiogram.

concepts: echo coinciding with next whistle, time interval
questions.question:
A boy standing in front of a wall produces two whistles per second. He notices that the sound of his whistling coincides with the echo. The echo is heard only once when whistling is stopped. Calculate the distance between the boy and the wall. (The speed of sound in air = 320 m/s)
(i) The time in which the boy hears the echo is
questions.solution: (b) 0.5 s. Whistles coincide with echo, so the echo returns in 0.5 s.

questions.question: (ii) The distance at which the boy is standing from the wall

concepts: echo time with changed speed and distance
questions.question: (iii) If the speed of sound is increased by 16 ms^-1 and the boy moves 4 m away from the wall then in how much time will he hear the echo of the first whistle?

concepts: 0.1 s persistence of hearing for echo
questions.question: (iv) In which of the following timings of reflection of the whistle, the echo cannot be heard?
questions.solution: (a) 0.05 s. To hear an echo the time difference should be at least 0.1 s.

concepts: speed of light in vacuum same for all wavelengths
questions.question: The ratio of velocities of light of wavelength 400 nm and 800 nm in a vacuum is
questions.solution: (a) 1 : 1. Velocity of light in vacuum is the same for all wavelengths.

questions.topic: KE vs mass at equal momentum
questions.question:
A light body A and a heavy body B have the same momentum.
(i) Choose a correct statement from the given options.

options.a: kinetic energy of body A and body B will be the same.
options.b: kinetic energy of body A is greater than kinetic energy of body B.
options.c: kinetic energy of body B is greater than kinetic energy of body A.
options.d: unless we know the velocity, we cannot find which body has greater kinetic energy.

questions.solution: (b) K.E. = p^2/2m, so K.E. is proportional to 1/m. Since mB > mA, K.E.A > K.E.B.

concepts: KE inversely proportional to mass at equal momentum
questions.question: (ii) If the ratio of kinetic energies of A and B is 5:2 then which one of the following gives the mass ratio of the bodies respectively?
questions.solution: (c) 2 : 5. K.E. is proportional to 1/m, so K.E.A/K.E.B = mB/mA = 5/2, hence mA/mB = 2/5.

concepts: angle of incidence measured from normal
questions.question:
The diagram below shows a ray of light travelling from air into a glass material (a block with a curved surface AD and flat surfaces AB, BC). Answer the questions that follow:
(i) The angle of incidence at the surface AB is
questions.solution: (b) 47°. Angle of incidence = 90° - 43° = 47°.
questions.figure_desc: Glass block with a curved surface AD and flat faces AB, BC. A ray enters the curved surface AD undeviated (along a radius), strikes AB where an angle of 43 degrees is marked with the surface, undergoes total internal reflection at F, then meets BC.

concepts: refraction at curved surface along radius, no deviation
questions.question: (ii) Select a correct statement from the following.

options.a: The speed of light at the curved surface AD does not change while entering the block.
options.b: The ray at the surface AD is not travelling along the radius of the curved part.
options.c: The ray at the surface AD is travelling along the radius of the curved part.
options.d: Light never refracts when it enters a curved surface.

questions.solution: (c) The ray at the surface AD is travelling along the radius of the curved part, since it is not deviated at AD.

concepts: geometry of angles in glass block, total internal reflection
questions.question: (iii) The angle of incidence on the surface BC is
questions.solution: (a) 43°. TIR occurs at F; angle EFB = 43 deg, FEB = 90 - 43 = 47 deg, so angle of incidence at BC = 90 - 47 = 43 deg.

concepts: finding critical angle from TIR diagram
questions.question: (iv) The critical angle of this material of glass
questions.solution: (b) 43°. TIR occurs at 47 deg at F, so critical angle is less than that; at BC the refracted ray grazes the surface, so the incidence angle 43 deg equals the critical angle.

concepts: total internal reflection in right-angled prism
questions.question:
The diagram below shows the path of light passing through a right-angled prism of critical angle 42°.
(i) The angle C of the prism is
questions.solution: (d) 30°. Angle of incidence (60 deg) > critical angle, TIR at D; angle ADE = 90 - 60 = 30 deg, so angle A = 60 deg; in triangle ABC, 60 + 90 + C = 180, so C = 30 deg.
questions.figure_desc: Right-angled prism ABC (angle B = 90 deg) with a ray entering one face, striking the hypotenuse side at D at 60 degrees incidence, and continuing.

concepts: ray path in prism with TIR then refraction
questions.question: (ii) Which one of the following diagrams shows the correct path of this ray till it emerges out of the prism?
questions.solution: (b). TIR occurs at D (60 deg > 42 deg), angle of reflection 60 deg; angle of incidence at F = 120 - 90 = 30 deg < critical angle, so regular refraction takes place and the ray emerges.
questions.figure_desc: Right-angled prism ABC with four candidate ray paths (a)-(d) drawn; the options are diagrams only. Correct (b): TIR at D, then refraction out at F.
